claims.text: Stable angina: used when symptoms persist despite beta-blockers, long-acting nitrates or CCBs;
claims.quote: Ranolazine is a sodium channel blocker that can be used to treat chronic angina in patients whose symptoms persist despite beta-blockers, long-acting nitrates, or calcium channel blockers (3).

claims.text: because it can prolong the QT interval, it is usually reserved for symptoms that persist on optimal other antianginal therapy.
claims.quote: Because ranolazine may cause QT interval prolongation, it is usually reserved for patients in whom symptoms persist despite optimal treatment with other antianginal agents.

claims.text: Dose: start 500 mg twice daily and increase to 1000 mg twice daily as needed;
claims.quote: Initiate ranolazine extended-release tablet dosing at 500 mg twice daily and increase to 1000 mg twice daily, as needed, based on clinical symptoms.
The maximum recommended daily dose of ranolazine extended-release tablet is 1000 mg twice daily.

claims.text: Also contraindicated with strong CYP3A inhibitors (eg, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, nelfinavir).
claims.quote: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, nelfinavir)

claims.text: Interactions: limit ranolazine to 500 mg twice daily with moderate CYP3A inhibitors (diltiazem, verapamil, erythromycin, fluconazole, grapefruit);
claims.quote: Limit the dose of ranolazine to 500 mg twice daily in patients on moderate CYP3A inhibitors, including diltiazem, verapamil, erythromycin, fluconazole, and grapefruit juice or grapefruit-containing products
claims.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on Ranolazine

claims.quote: Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on any dose of ranolazine to 20 mg once daily
claims.locator: 7.2 Effects of Ranolazine on Other Drugs

claims.text: with ranolazine 1000 mg twice daily, metformin should not exceed 1700 mg/day.
claims.quote: When ranolazine 1000 mg twice daily is co-administered with metformin, metformin dose should not exceed 1700 mg/day.
claims.locator: 7.2 Effects of Ranolazine on Other Drugs

claims.text: Monitor renal function periodically with moderate to severe renal impairment; stop it if acute renal failure develops.
claims.quote: Monitor renal function periodically in patients with moderate to severe renal impairment. Discontinue ranolazine if acute renal failure develops.
claims.locator: 8.7 Use in Patients with Renal Impairment

claims.text: Counseling: take with or without meals;
claims.quote: Take ranolazine extended-release tablet with or without meals.

claims.text: swallow whole, don't crush, break or chew.
claims.quote: Swallow ranolazine extended-release tablet whole; do not crush, break, or chew.

claims.text: Overdose: hypotension, QT prolongation, bradycardia, myoclonus, severe tremor, dizziness, nausea/vomiting and hallucinations;
claims.quote: Hypotension, QT prolongation, bradycardia, myoclonic activity, severe tremor, unsteady gait/incoordination, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, dysphasia, and hallucinations have been seen in cases of oral overdose of ranolazine.

claims.text: supportive care, and continuous ECG monitoring may be warranted.
claims.quote: In addition to general supportive measures, continuous ECG monitoring may be warranted in the event of overdose.
